posts.text:
So it turns out that Ukraine's issues with Starlink were caused by Ukraine.

Starlink terminals disconnected at speeds above 160 KPH, as determined by the Starlink terminals internal GPS.

To get around this, Ukraine hacked the Starlink terminals to think they were stationary regardless of speed.

SpaceX figured this out, and updated the system software to detect excessive speed by seeing how rapidly the terminal switched from on satellite to another.  This broke Ukraine's hack, and Starlink would no longer work at high speeds.

Ukraine was using Starlink in a way that violated the terms of service.

Starlink figured it out and stopped it.

posts.text:
AMAZON $AMZN CEO ANDY JASSY SAYS AWS IS SOLD OUT FOR 2026 AND LARGELY SOLD OUT FOR 2027

And a good chunk of 2028 is already gone too

"'26 is obviously at this point sold out. '27 is largely sold out. We always leave a certain amount for on demand in our inference service Bedrock or EC2, but largely sold out. All the big chunks. A good chunk of '28 is sold out."

He said that's why Amazon can invest a lot more in capacity without it being a bad use of capital.

"There's only so much data center and power today. There's only so much memory, and I don't think that shortage ends in 2027."

He said both AWS's AI business and its core non-AI business are "growing at really rapid rates right now," which forces tough calls on how much memory goes to AI chips versus everything else.

"These are real trade-offs you have to make."

INVESTORS WOULD BE BARRED FROM BUYING UP SINGLE-FAMILY HOMES UNDER NEW US TREASURY RULE

The US Treasury is issuing a proposed federal rule on Thursday to implement one of President Trump’s signature housing affordability bills that would bar institutional investors from buying single-family homes.

In a notice of proposed rulemaking, the Treasury Department will propose regulations prohibiting investors from purchasing the homes starting on Jan. 7, 2027 — unless it’s identified as an “excepted purchase,” such as those involved in build-to-rent programs, renovate-to-rent programs and homeownership programs.

“Under President Trump, this Administration continues to restore the path to affordable homeownership for millions of young and working families,” said Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent in a statement.
